spec_notes: The specification does not contradict the request; every stated item has a clause (C-1 to C-51). It marks as Open the handling of malformed or inconsistent FENs (C-4), non-UCI or non-string moves (C-26), test fixtures and depths beyond start depth 2 (C-49) and the benchmark conditions (C-50, C-51). It decides without marking that castling needs the king and rook on their home squares whatever the rights field says (C-18) and that en passant needs the passed pawn alongside (C-19), and that a saved FEN is reused independently of call order (C-4, C-55). Discovery clauses C-52 to C-59 pin outcomes a correct product shares (en-passant as sole escape, both-rights revocation, repetition and 50-move counts not changing status, bare kings 'ongoing'); C-20 'the move without a suffix is absent' pins rejection of a bare promotion, which the inventory also allows to be read as a queen if documented. It says nothing about IllegalMoveError's message, name or base class.
tests_notes: Several tests combine behaviours: 'applying a move uses the supplied snapshot...' covers startFen, illegal-move rejection, en-passant target, halfmove and fullmove at once; 'status distinguishes a playable check and a stalemate' covers check, ongoing, stalemate and an illegal move; the en-passant tests mix capture, expiry, pins and snapshot reuse. The timing test depends on machine speed (generous margins, warms up first). All IllegalMoveError assertions use the imported class as the assert.throws validator, so removing the export leaves the suite green (proved). No test covers an invalid FEN or a non-string move. 'promotion offers four sorted choices...' asserts that bare 'e7e8' throws, which would fail on another correct build that documents a bare promotion as a queen. No tests are tied to internals (only the public API is called).
maintainer: Move legality hinges on one generator (legalCandidates) shared by legalMoves, status and applyMove, and applyMove finds a move by regenerating every legal move and comparing UCI strings, so any change to move generation or toUci silently changes which inputs are accepted. Castling and rights use hard-coded 0-63 square indices (CASTLES table, kingFrom 60, rookFrom 63 and so on) and remainingRights reads the pre-move board, which makes it easy to break revocation on corner captures; the depth-2 suite would not catch a depth-3 regression.
